summary: Every published recipient public key names its suite. Frozen contracts that publish a raw 32-byte X25519 key get a successor version with an explicit suite field; their existing objects stay readable while the suite is read-only.
rule: A sender selects the suite from the recipient key's publication, never from configuration or the envelope. Sealing to a key whose suite is not active fails with key-migration-pending; the recipient owner must publish an active-suite key first.

publications.object: Member and Agent key directory entries

publications.migration: An unlocked member client publishes the next manifest revision with a new X-Wing vault agent message key (agentMessageKeyVersion + 1), keeping the previous private key in the Vault's encrypted key material until no pending reason addresses it.
publications.legacy: manifests without the field carry an X25519 key; they verify and open but are never sealed to

publications.migration: An approver client performs the existing keyVersion + 1 rotation with continuitySignature; the new message key is X-Wing.
publications.legacy: v1 manifests stay verifiable; pending v1 submissions are re-wrapped by the Agent for the new key version through the existing re-wrap path

publications.wrapperContext: each wrapped DEK uses its own suite id in the key-wrapper context (purpose 7); the suite must equal the recipient key publication's suite
publications.legacy: v1 submissions stay decidable while palladin-x25519-sealed-box-v1 is read-only

publications.object: Grant envelopes (vault-v2 GrantDEK, purpose 4), Agent Vault key (purpose 5), Agent discovery key (purpose 2) and Script execution packages (script-execution v1, purpose 6)
publications.wrapperContext: the wrapper suite equals the recipient Agent key publication's suite; contracts that name palladin-x25519-sealed-box-v1 as a constant are superseded for new writes
